entry.title: Atomicity - Design a Reliable Wallet Transfer System with ACID Guarantees
entry.summary:
Atomicity in Action: Designing a Reliable Wallet Transfer System with ACID Guarantees
Building a wallet system like PhonePe, GPay, or Paytm requires strict data consistency. Even a small error can lead to money loss, duplicate transactions, or incorrect balances. This is why ACID properties, especially Atomicity, are critical in such systems. Atomicity ensures that all operations in a transaction are completed successfully. If any step fails, the entire transaction is rolled back, and the database remains unchanged. CREATE TABLE accounts ( Insert sample data: INSERT INTO accounts (name, balance) Initial state of the table:
ID Name Balance
1 Alice 1000
2 Bob 500
Transfer 200 from Alice to Bob using a transaction: UPDATE accounts UPDATE accounts After execution:
Name Balance
Alice 800
Bob 700
Both operations succeed, and the transaction is committed. The data remains consistent. Now introduce an error after deducting money from Alice: BEGIN; UPDATE accounts UPDATE accounts The second query fails due to an invalid column name. The database aborts the transaction. Final state:
Name Balance
Alice 1000
Bob 500
The deduction from Alice is rolled back. No partial update occurs. UPDATE accounts ROLLBACK; Final state remains unchanged:
Name Balance
Alice 1000
Bob 500
The rollback cancels all changes made during the transaction. If the same operations are executed without a transaction: UPDATE accounts UPDATE accounts Alice’s balance is reduced, but Bob does not receive the money. This leads to inconsistency. Transactions ensure all operations are executed completely or not at all. Atomicity guarantees that a transaction is treated as a single unit of work. In a wallet system, this ensures that money is neither lost nor duplicated. By using transaction blocks, the system remains consistent even in the presence of failures.
